points.description: First valid difference stated precisely and correctly, with the correct technical terms (e.g. UDP header is 8 bytes / short and fixed-length, while TCP header is 20-60 bytes / variable-length).

Second distinct valid difference stated precisely and correctly. Valid differences: UDP fixed vs TCP variable header length; TCP-only fields (sequence number, acknowledgment number, reserved, flags/control bits, advertised window, urgent pointer, options + padding); UDP has a packet length field (header + data) while TCP has header length/data offset (header only); source port optional in UDP but necessary in TCP.
Third distinct valid difference stated precisely and correctly, using the correct field names.
Fourth distinct valid difference stated precisely and correctly, using the correct field names. No wrong statements among the four.

rubric.notes: Each of four distinct, correct differences earns 0.25; the student must give at least four. Naming a TCP-only field counts as one difference per field only if it is a real field in the model answer (e.g. sequence number, window); vague statements like "TCP has more fields" earn nothing. A wrong claim (e.g. UDP has a sequence number, wrong header sizes) cancels that point. Repeating the same difference in different words counts once.
